classification.difficultyReason: Translate each stated relationship into a taught circle arrangement, preserving subset direction and showing overlap without containment when neither set is a subset.

content.prompt: Draw a Venn diagram to illustrate each situation, where $A$ and $B$ are subsets of the universal set $E$.

answer.short: $A$ lies entirely inside $B$, with both inside $E$.
answer.worked: Draw a rectangle labelled $E$. Draw a circle labelled $B$ inside it, then a smaller circle labelled $A$ entirely inside $B$. Every element of $A$ is therefore in $B$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6a; answer figure on teacher PDF page 75
spec.description: An A circle wholly inside a larger B circle, both inside rectangle E; ordinary outlines and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: A is a subset of B.

answer.short: $B$ lies entirely inside $A$, with both inside $E$.
answer.worked: Draw a rectangle labelled $E$. Draw a circle labelled $A$ inside it, then a smaller circle labelled $B$ entirely inside $A$. Every element of $B$ is therefore in $A$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6b; answer figure on teacher PDF page 75
spec.description: A B circle wholly inside a larger A circle, both inside rectangle E.
spec.mathematics: B is a subset of A.

answer.worked: Draw a rectangle labelled $E$ containing two separate circles labelled $A$ and $B$. The circles do not overlap because disjoint sets have no common elements: $A\cap B=\varnothing$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6c; answer figure on teacher PDF page 75
spec.description: Two separate circles A and B inside rectangle E.
spec.mathematics: A and B are disjoint; their intersection is empty.

children.label: d
children.prompt: $A$ and $B$ have some common elements but neither set is a subset of the other.

answer.short: Overlapping circles $A$ and $B$ inside $E$, with part of each circle outside the other.
answer.worked: Draw a rectangle labelled $E$ containing two overlapping circles labelled $A$ and $B$. Their overlap represents common elements. Leave a region of each circle outside the other, so neither set is a subset of the other.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6d; answer figure on teacher PDF page 75
spec.description: Overlapping circles A and B inside rectangle E, with nonempty exclusive regions on both sides.
spec.mathematics: The sets share elements, and neither contains the other.
